panels.title: Transaction Processing Rate
panels.description:
**What:** Rate of transactions entering the processing pipeline (submitted locally or relayed by peers) versus raw transaction messages arriving from peers before deduplication.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of each over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** The received line sits above the processed line by the volume of duplicates filtered out.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; scales with network transaction volume.
**Watch for:** A large and growing gap means heavy duplicate traffic; a processed-rate collapse means submissions are not being handled.
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp:NetworkOPsImp::processTransaction, src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp:PeerImp::handleTransaction

targets.expr: sum by (service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="tx.process", tx_type=~"$tx_type"}[$__rate_interval]))

sum by (service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="tx.receive", tx_type=~"$tx_type"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Transaction Processing Latency by Type
panels.description:
**What:** Per-transaction-type processing latency through the pipeline.
**How it's computed:** 95th and 50th percentile of per-type durations over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Simple payments are fast; complex types like offers or AMM operations run longer.
**Healthy range:** Sub-millisecond to a few milliseconds; type-dependent.
**Watch for:** A latency climb for one type signals contention or expensive processing specific to it.
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp:NetworkOPsImp::processTransaction

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, tx_type, service_instance_id) (rate(span_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="tx.process", tx_type=~"$tx_type"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le, tx_type, service_instance_id) (rate(span_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="tx.process", tx_type=~"$tx_type"}[5m])))

panels.title: Transaction Path Distribution
panels.description:
**What:** Split of processed transactions by origin: submitted locally versus relayed from peers.
**How it's computed:** Total counts split by origin over a 5-minute window, shown as proportions.
**Reading it:** Most nodes see mostly relayed traffic; a submission endpoint sees more local.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** A surge in local submissions on a node not meant to accept them can indicate misuse.
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp:NetworkOPsImp::processTransaction

targets.expr: sum by (local, service_instance_id) (increase(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", local=~"$tx_origin", span_name="tx.process", tx_type=~"$tx_type"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Transaction Receive vs Suppressed
panels.description:
**What:** Raw transaction messages received from peers, split by whether they were suppressed as duplicates before processing.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate split by suppressed flag over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** A healthy relay network produces a steady suppressed share as duplicates are filtered.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; suppression is expected and normal.
**Watch for:** A sharp rise in the suppressed line can reflect gossip amplification or a peer replaying transactions.
**Source:** src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp:PeerImp::handleTransaction

targets.expr: sum by (suppressed, service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{span_name="tx.receive", tx_type=~"$tx_type", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Transaction Processing Duration Heatmap
panels.description:
**What:** Distribution of transaction processing times over time.
**How it's computed:** Counts of transactions by duration band in each 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** A single tight band is healthy; brighter cells mark the common processing time.
**Healthy range:** Concentrated at low latency.
**Watch for:** A second high-latency band reveals a subset of transactions that are consistently slow.
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp:NetworkOPsImp::processTransaction

targets.expr: sum(increase(span_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="tx.process", tx_type=~"$tx_type"}[5m])) by (le)

panels.title: Transaction Apply Duration per Ledger
panels.description:
**What:** Time to apply the agreed transaction set into a new ledger.
**How it's computed:** 95th and 50th percentile of per-ledger apply durations over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Scales with the number and complexity of transactions per ledger.
**Healthy range:** Tens to a few hundred milliseconds under normal load.
**Watch for:** Sustained high durations indicate heavy transaction sets or expensive processing.
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/ledger/detail/BuildLedger.cpp:applyTransactions

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service_instance_id) (rate(span_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="tx.apply"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le, service_instance_id) (rate(span_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="tx.apply"}[5m])))

panels.title: Transaction Apply Failed Rate
panels.description:
**What:** Rate of transactor-stage applies that returned a non-success result while building a ledger.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of tx.transactor spans at stage=apply whose ter_result is not tesSUCCESS, per node.
**Reading it:** Green below 1/s, yellow 1-5/s, red above 5/s.
**Healthy range:** A steady low non-zero rate is normal (e.g. tefPAST_SEQ, tecUNFUNDED and other benign conflicts).
**Watch for:** A sustained jump above the normal baseline can indicate malformed transaction floods or a systemic issue.
**Source:** src/libxrpl/tx/Transactor.cpp:Transactor::operator()

targets.expr: sum by (service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="tx.transactor", stage="apply", ter_result!~"tesSUCCESS|"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Transaction Rate by Type
panels.description:
**What:** Processing rate broken down by transaction type (Payment, OfferCreate, AMM operations, etc.).
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate per type over a 5-minute window.
**Reading it:** Shows the transaction mix and how it shifts over time.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; usually Payment-heavy.
**Watch for:** A sudden burst of one type is a leading indicator of spam or fee escalation.
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp:NetworkOPsImp::processTransaction

targets.expr: sum by (tx_type) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="tx.process", tx_type=~"$tx_type"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Transaction Results by Type
panels.description:
**What:** Non-success result codes broken down by transaction type, showing which types fail and how.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate per type and result code over a 5-minute window (successes excluded).
**Reading it:** Occasional failures are normal; watch which types and codes dominate.
**Healthy range:** Low and workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** A concentration of one failure code on one type can indicate a broken client or targeted spam.
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp:NetworkOPsImp::processTransaction

targets.expr: sum by (tx_type, ter_result) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="tx.process", tx_type=~"$tx_type", ter_result=~"$ter_result", ter_result!="tesSUCCESS"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: TxQ Accept: Applied Ratio per Node (State Timeline)
panels.description:
**What:** Applied fraction of TxQ accepts per node over time: the share of queued transactions that were included in a ledger versus removed on failure.
**How it's computed:** Per node, applied accepts divided by applied-plus-failed accepts over a 5-minute window.
**Reading it:** Green (>=90% applied) is a healthy drain; yellow is degraded; red means accepts are mostly failing.
**Healthy range:** At or near 100% applied when the queue is draining healthily; workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** A node dropping into yellow or red, which signals queue pressure, under-bidding, or fee escalation on that node.
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/TxQ.cpp:TxQ::accept

targets.expr:
sum by (service_instance_id) (increase(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="txq.accept_tx", txq_status="applied"}[$__rate_interval]))
/
sum by (service_instance_id) (increase(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="txq.accept_tx", txq_status=~"applied|failed"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Transactor Duration by Type (p95)
panels.description:
**What:** Per-type execution time of the transactor that actually applies each transaction's effects.
**How it's computed:** 95th percentile of per-type durations over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Reveals which transaction types are most expensive to execute.
**Healthy range:** Sub-millisecond to a few milliseconds; type-dependent.
**Watch for:** A climbing figure for one type points to expensive processing or contention for that type.
**Source:** src/libxrpl/tx/Transactor.cpp:Transactor::operator()

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, tx_type, service_instance_id) (rate(span_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="tx.transactor", tx_type=~"$tx_type"}[5m])))

panels.title: TxQ Enqueue Rate by Transaction Type
panels.description:
**What:** Rate at which transactions are placed into the queue, split by transaction type.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate per type over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Shows which types make up inbound demand and how the mix shifts as the queue fills.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** A spam burst of one type here is a leading indicator of fee escalation.
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/TxQ.cpp:TxQ::apply

targets.expr: sum by (tx_type, service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="txq.enqueue"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Queue Accept (Drain) Duration per Ledger
panels.description:
**What:** Time spent draining queued transactions into a newly closed ledger.
**How it's computed:** 95th and 50th percentile of per-ledger drain durations over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Rises as the queue holds more transactions to process at close.
**Healthy range:** A few milliseconds when the queue is light.
**Watch for:** Rising drain time signals queue pressure at ledger close.
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/TxQ.cpp:TxQ::accept

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service_instance_id) (rate(span_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="txq.accept"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le, service_instance_id) (rate(span_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="txq.accept"}[5m])))

panels.title: Queue Cleanup Rate (Expired Entries)
panels.description:
**What:** Rate at which expired transactions are removed from the queue each ledger.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Normally low; entries expire when submitters underbid the current fee.
**Healthy range:** Near zero in calm conditions.
**Watch for:** A rising rate means submitters abandoned under-fee transactions, a demand-frustration signal distinct from throughput.
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/TxQ.cpp:TxQ::processClosedLedger

targets.expr: sum by (service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="txq.cleanup"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Tx Apply Pipeline Rate by Stage
panels.description:
**What:** Throughput of each apply-pipeline stage (preflight, preclaim, apply), showing where transactions drop out.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate per stage over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** A decline from earlier to later stages shows where transactions are filtered.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; later stages sit at or below earlier ones.
**Watch for:** A large early-stage drop means many transactions fail basic checks, consistent with malformed floods.
**Source:** src/libxrpl/tx/Transactor.cpp:Transactor::operator()

targets.expr: sum by (stage, service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name=~"tx.preflight|tx.preclaim|tx.transactor", stage=~"$stage"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Tx Apply Pipeline Latency by Stage (p95)
panels.description:
**What:** 95th-percentile duration of each apply-pipeline stage (preflight, preclaim, apply).
**How it's computed:** 95th percentile of per-stage durations over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Isolates which stage dominates transaction processing time.
**Healthy range:** Sub-millisecond to a few milliseconds per stage.
**Watch for:** A stage that grows disproportionately points to a bottleneck in that step.
**Source:** src/libxrpl/tx/Transactor.cpp:Transactor::operator()

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, stage, service_instance_id) (rate(span_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name=~"tx.preflight|tx.preclaim|tx.transactor", stage=~"$stage"}[5m])))

panels.title: Tx Apply Pipeline Failure Rate by Stage
panels.description:
**What:** Rate of pipeline spans ending in a non-success result, split by stage (preflight, preclaim, apply).
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of non-success outcomes per stage over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Shows whether failures concentrate early (basic checks) or late (application).
**Healthy range:** Low and workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** A surge of early-stage failures is consistent with malformed or spam transaction floods.
**Source:** src/libxrpl/tx/Transactor.cpp:Transactor::operator()

targets.expr: sum by (stage, service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name=~"tx.preflight|tx.preclaim|tx.transactor", stage=~"$stage", ter_result!~"tesSUCCESS|"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Tx Apply Pipeline Latency by Type and Stage (p95)
panels.description:
**What:** 95th-percentile stage duration broken down by both transaction type and pipeline stage.
**How it's computed:** 95th percentile of durations per type and stage over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** For each transaction type, shows which stage dominates its latency.
**Healthy range:** Sub-millisecond to a few milliseconds; type- and stage-dependent.
**Watch for:** A specific type-and-stage combination climbing points to a targeted expensive or abusive pattern.
**Source:** src/libxrpl/tx/Transactor.cpp:Transactor::operator()

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, tx_type, stage, service_instance_id) (rate(span_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name=~"tx.preflight|tx.preclaim|tx.transactor", tx_type=~"$tx_type", stage=~"$stage"}[5m])))
